Insightful mechanistic analysis identifying key properties (a_t ≈ 1 for maintaining full state information, convolution window w ≥ k+1 requirement) with clear empirical validation (Figs. 4-5)
Strong experimental practices including grid search over hyperparameters, detailed appendix with full specifications, extensions to non-Markovian data (switching Markov), and promised code release
Fundamental lower bound (Theorem 2) establishing exponential scaling of hidden dimension with Markov order, providing theoretical grounding for architectural requirements
weaknesses: Severely limited theoretical scope: Theorem 1 only covers first-order Markov chains (k=1), while higher orders lack theoretical justification and rely solely on empirical evidence (Figs. 1b, 3b), contradicting the paper's general title

strengths: Novel theoretical contribution: First formal connection between Mamba and optimal statistical estimators (Laplacian smoothing), filling an important gap in understanding SSMs

Fundamental theoretical insights: Theorem 1 proves exact representation capability for first-order Markov; Theorem 2 establishes Ω(2^k) lower bound on hidden dimension across all recurrent depths
Comprehensive ablation studies: Clearly demonstrate convolution's centrality—model fails without it, succeeds with only convolution (MambaZero)—going beyond typical ablations
Clear mechanistic insights: Identifying convolution (over gating/nonlinearity) as the key component provides actionable understanding for architecture design
Rigorous experimental methodology: Proper baselines (transformers, linear attention), multiple runs with error bars, grid search over hyperparameters, consistent across varying depths/state spaces
